The first draft initiated by eng Mohammed Aly Aly Hassan at El_Shabab Gas power 
station and tested at 21 May 2002, East Delta Company for Electricity.

A work permit
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
 safety category,

Safety fence
 (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area,

items:
No smoking is 
 perminted in battery room

Use standard 
 personal safety equipment, goggles, rubber gloves, rubber apron.

Do not place 
 any tools on top of battery cells (danger of short circuit)

Never use the 
 same tools on lead cells you may have used before on alkaline cells

Complete 
 toolset, Digital voltmeter, hydrometer, and glove.

Read overall 
 voltage of bank and record on battery maintenance card,

Disconnect AC 
 supply to battery charger,

Inspect the 
 outside of cells for cracks and leakage of electrolyte

If you 
 discover defective cell use the recommended procedure to replace with a new 
 cell

Inspect 
 electrolyte level and record density for each cell, add distilled water if 
 level is below normal

Inspect inter 
 - cell connection and terminals of cells and clean any salt deposits with 
 distilled water

Check terminal 
 connection for tightness

Lubricate 
 terminals of cells with a thin film of vaseline

Clean top of 
 cells

Read voltage 
 per cell and record on battery maintenance card

Check 
 ventilation system

Again read 
 overall voltage of bank and record on battery maintenance card and compare 
 the reading from step No1

If overall 
 voltage is below 125V place battery bank on (high) charge for 4:5 
 hours after which the charger back on normal charge

Compare the 
 present readings with the last readings

Inspect 
 visually for SCR, diod and capacitors

Power Stations
Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document out 
lines the battery inspection I1 to be performed an a monthly bases M1 as 
indicated in the above title block
The first draft initiated by eng Mohammed Aly Aly Hassan at El_Shabab Gas power 
station and tested at 21 May 2002, East Delta Company for Electricity.
Safety 
Precautions
A work permit
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
 safety category,
Safety fence
 (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area,
No smoking is 
 perminted in battery room
Use standard 
 personal safety equipment, goggles, rubber gloves, rubber apron.
Do not place 
 any tools on top of battery cells (danger of short circuit)
Never use the 
 same tools on lead cells you may have used before on alkaline cells
Tools and Equipments
Complete 
 toolset, Digital voltmeter, hydrometer, and glove.
Work to be carried out
Read overall 
 voltage of bank and record on battery maintenance card,
Disconnect AC 
 supply to battery charger,
Inspect the 
 outside of cells for cracks and leakage of electrolyte
If you 
 discover defective cell use the recommended procedure to replace with a new 
 cell
Inspect 
 electrolyte level and record density for each cell, add distilled water if 
 level is below normal
Inspect inter 
 - cell connection and terminals of cells and clean any salt deposits with 
 distilled water
Check terminal 
 connection for tightness
Lubricate 
 terminals of cells with a thin film of vaseline
Clean top of 
 cells
Read voltage 
 per cell and record on battery maintenance card
Check 
 ventilation system
Again read 
 overall voltage of bank and record on battery maintenance card and compare 
 the reading from step No1
If overall 
 voltage is below 125V place battery bank on (high) charge for 4:5 
 hours after which the charger back on normal charge
Compare the 
 present readings with the last readings
Inspect 
 visually for SCR, diod and capacitors
